Founder: We integrate with Gmail's APIs (not IMAP) to enable faster real-time updates, better latency compensation, offline handling, bundled inboxes, and emoji reactions.

User: 'This layout and color palette are strongly evocative of Inbox... I'd presume you're trying to recreate Inbox.' Founder confirmed: 'Many of us were Inbox users and miss it! We're trying to do more than Inbox did, but we were certainly inspired by it.'
User complaint: 'all these apps either want gmail way too many gmail permissions, and/or are hosted... I'm trying to get rid of gmail lol.'

Front power-user praised Shortwave's 'Bundles' grouping feature as 'top shelf,' better than Front's tags/folders, though he found Workspaces uninteresting and wasn't sure Bundles could replace Team Inboxes.

User feedback: 'you can't do much worse than the default gmail interface... What I liked less is the tiny print and tiny UI elements of shortwave in general... the typography could use some attention.'
Privacy concern: user worried about syncing sensitive emails (OTPs, bank/SSN emails) to Shortwave's servers and wished for a denylist to exclude certain mail from syncing.
User quoted privacy policy allowing sharing of email content/metadata with third-party vendors and said 'Hard pass' given business email confidentiality concerns.

'I must say I loved it. In 10min I cleared my inbox which I was postponing for a few weeks... it imported all my aliases and signatures.' User also liked that deleting the Shortwave account made switching back to Gmail low-risk.

Pricing pushback: 'The pricing does not really make sense for personal user ($9/mo for a email client).' Another compared it unfavorably to Superhuman's $30/mo, asking for differentiators given Shortwave targets teams/enterprise.

Free plan limitation noted: emails from more than 90 days before signup aren't imported for search, and snoozed emails past that window won't show up in search results (though they still arrive in the inbox).

Security-focused user: 'there is no way I could use a web mail client for security reasons (as a security consultant, we use PGP a lot and need a local email provider)... it only works with Google servers.'

HN commenter skeptical of longevity: 'Can't wait for them to get acquihired out of existence just like every other email startup,' to which the founder replied he previously sold Firebase to Google and doesn't plan to repeat that.
TechCrunch reported Shortwave introduced AI-powered email summaries, prompting HN discussion about whether AI-summarized emails signal 'the death of email.'
Security vendor blog highlighted that Shortwave's AI Email with MCP integration 'opens up rich capabilities—but also new attack surfaces,' framing it as a potential phishing target ('white whale').
